title: Commissions and Committees of the Indian Statistical System
breadcrumb: Official Statistics → Indian Statistical System → Commissions and committees
engineName: Institutions and official statistics — who reviewed what, and what came of it
provenance: Re-audited on 14 November 2026 against official MoSPI, Parliament/PIB and India Code sources. MoSPI's 2025 chronology fixes the Bowley–Robertson appointment at 1934. The National Income Committee's final report and MoSPI annual reports support its 1949 constitution, chair and members, and the April 1951 / February 1954 reports. MoSPI's NSC annual report supports the Rangarajan Commission's August 2001 report date and the first NSC's 2006 constitution under Prof. Suresh D. Tendulkar. The Collection of Statistics (Amendment) Act 2017 was checked against its official text. A MoSPI Lok Sabha reply dated 24 July 2024 confirms the NSS Steering Committee's 14 June 2024 order, 17 members and two-year original tenure. No primary order confirming the SCoS dissolution or a post-June 2026 extension/reconstitution was located; those claims are not retained as facts.
objectives: Name the four landmark reviews of the Indian statistical system with their chairs and years.
State what the Rangarajan Commission recommended and which recommendations were and were not implemented.
Put the five poverty estimation committees in order and say what each changed.
Distinguish the two Rangarajan bodies, and recognise Tendulkar in both of his roles.
State what the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 does and the three changes made by the 2017 amendment.
Describe the 2024 Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys from the official MoSPI order, and distinguish what is known from what remains unverified.

sheet: Bowley–Robertson Committee: appointed 1934; recommended one coordinating agency and provincial statisticians.
National Income Committee 1949: Mahalanobis (chair), Gadgil, V. K. R. V. Rao. First report April 1951, final 1954.
The National Income Committee's work contributed to the development of national accounts and central statistical coordination; do not present it as the sole cause of the CSO.
Rangarajan Commission: constituted early 2000, report submitted August 2001.
It recommended a statutory apex body accountable to Parliament, a professional National Statistician, regular statistical audits and reform of the Collection of Statistics Act.

Implementation distinction: the official professional post is Chief Statistician of India (CSI); the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 replaced the 1953 Act and was amended in 2017. The NSC was created by resolution, not statute. Its 2019 mandate includes statistical audit, but a regular audit cycle was not verified.
NSC created by resolution 1 June 2005, effective 2006; first chairman Suresh Tendulkar.
Poverty: Dandekar–Rath 1971 (2,250 calories), Alagh 1979, Lakdawala 1993 (state-specific, CPI-IW and CPI-AL, adopted 1997), Tendulkar 2009 (no calorie anchor), Rangarajan 2014 (29.5% in 2011-12).
Collection of Statistics Act 2008 replaced the 1953 Act.
The 2017 amendment: jurisdiction extended with a J&K proviso; section 3A on nodal officers; section 9(1) on use of information. It did not change penalties and did not make the NSC statutory.

The original two-year tenure reached its end in June 2026; no official extension or reconstitution order was located by 14 November 2026. Do not claim current status or direct succession to all SCoS functions without a new primary order.
C. Rangarajan chaired two different bodies: the 2000–01 statistical system commission and the 2012–14 poverty group.

scenes.title: Before the lesson — four things it will assume
scenes.objective: Separate the kinds of body that recur here, and know what a report can and cannot do.
body: This topic is a list of names, years and chairpersons, and the only way it goes wrong is if the categories blur. A committee is not a commission, a recommendation is not a law, and a body that was renamed is not a body that was replaced.
Four checks. Each one is a distinction that a question will be built on, and each takes a minute.

items.ask: What is the difference between a committee, a commission and a working group?
items.recall: In Indian official practice these are degrees of standing rather than sharply defined legal forms. A working group is usually small, internal and tasked with one question; a committee is appointed for a defined subject and reports; a commission is the weightiest, usually chaired by an eminent outsider and reviewing a whole system. None of the three is automatically statutory.
refresh: The labels matter for the exam because questions quote them exactly. The Rangarajan body that reviewed the statistical system in 2000-01 is called a Commission; the bodies that have fixed poverty lines are called Committees or Expert Groups; the bodies inside the Planning Commission that did preparatory work were Task Forces and Working Groups.
What they share is that they advise. Whether their advice becomes binding depends entirely on whether the government acts on it, which is the theme of this whole topic.

One practical rule: if a body has a chairperson who is a serving official and a one-line remit, it is a working group; if it is chaired by a former governor or a professor and reviews a system, it is a commission.

items.ask: What does it mean that a committee 'recommended' something?
items.recall: That it put the proposal in its report. Nothing follows automatically. A recommendation becomes real only when the government accepts it and issues a resolution, a rule or an Act — and governments accept some recommendations and quietly drop others.
refresh: The clearest example in this topic is the Rangarajan Commission of 2001. It recommended a statutory apex body accountable to Parliament, a professional statistician as the ministry's Secretary, regular statistical audits, and a reformed Collection of Statistics Act.

What actually happened: the professional statistician post was created, the Act was reformed in 2008, and the statutory body never arrived — the National Statistical Commission exists, but by resolution and without statutory backing. Regular audits were not instituted.
So a question asking 'which of the following did the Rangarajan Commission recommend' and one asking 'which was implemented' have different answers, and the paper knows it.

items.ask: What is a poverty line, and why does fixing one need a committee?
items.recall: A poverty line is a level of consumption expenditure below which a household is counted as poor. It needs a committee because every element of it is a judgement: which basket of goods, which calorie norm if any, which price index to update it with, and whether rural and urban lines should be derived separately.
refresh: The oldest Indian approach anchored the line to a calorie requirement — famously 2,250 calories a day in the Dandekar–Rath work — and then asked what expenditure buys that in practice.

Later committees moved away from calories towards a broader basket including health and education, and changed the price indices used to update the line over time. Each change moves the headcount, sometimes by tens of millions of people, without anybody's actual consumption changing.

That is why the chairs of these committees are household names in Indian economics and why the sequence of them is examinable: the poverty number is a methodological artefact as much as a measurement.

items.ask: What is the National Sample Survey, and why do committees keep being appointed over it?
items.recall: The NSS is the large household and enterprise survey system run by the NSS wing of the NSO, in numbered rounds since 1950. Committees are appointed over it because its design decisions — sampling, questionnaire, reference period, tabulation — determine the official figures for consumption, employment and poverty.
refresh: If you change the recall period over which a household is asked to report its spending, you change measured consumption and therefore measured poverty. If you change the sampling frame you change who is represented.

So the technical committees that advise on survey design are not administrative detail: they are where the numbers are really made, which is why their composition, and who chairs them, becomes a public question.
This is the thread that runs from the National Income Committee of 1949 to the committees of the 2020s.

scenes.title: Why a statistical system keeps appointing committees
scenes.objective: See the committees as a single argument conducted over seventy years, not a list to memorise.
body: A statistical office faces a problem no other arm of government has. It must produce numbers that the government of the day may not like, using methods that only a few hundred people in the country can evaluate, on a budget that the same government sets.

Every committee in this topic is an attempt to answer one question: who guards the credibility of official numbers? The answers offered have been an expert review every few decades, a permanent commission, a statute, a professional statistician at the top of the ministry, and standing technical committees over survey design.

Read the sequence that way and the names stop being arbitrary. Bowley and Robertson in the 1930s asked for a single agency and provincial statisticians. Mahalanobis's National Income Committee in 1949 built the national accounts. The Rangarajan Commission in 2001 asked for an independent statutory commission. Each answer was partly implemented and the question came back.

For the exam, carry the official order date, composition and notified remit. For understanding, note that advisory and survey-specific committees are created for defined purposes and periods; their legal status and continuation must be checked against the relevant order rather than inferred from secondary reports.

aside.h: The sentence to carry into the exam
aside.body: Review bodies recommend; only governments implement. Every question in this topic that feels like a trick is really testing whether you know the difference.

ask.q: Why might a government prefer an advisory committee to a statutory commission, even when it says it wants credible statistics?
ask.nudge: Ask what each costs the government in control, and what each offers in credibility.

scenes.title: The four landmark reviews
scenes.objective: Place Bowley–Robertson, the National Income Committee, the Rangarajan Commission and the first NSC with their chairs.

blocks.body: MoSPI's 2025 official chronology dates the Bowley–Robertson Committee to 1934. Bowley and Robertson proposed a single agency to coordinate population and economic census work and statisticians in the provinces. Use 1934 as the official chronology date rather than repeating the unresolved 1933/1934 hedge.

blocks.h: The National Income Committee, 1949 — Mahalanobis, Gadgil, Rao
blocks.body: Set up in 1949, chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis, with D. R. Gadgil and V. K. R. V. Rao as members. Its first report came in April 1951 and its final report in February 1954. The Committee contributed to the development of national accounts and central statistical coordination; avoid saying it was the sole cause of the CSO's creation.

Constituted in early 2000 under Dr C. Rangarajan, former Governor of the Reserve Bank; its report was submitted in August 2001. It recommended a statutory apex body accountable to Parliament, a professional National Statistician, regular statistical audits, and reform of the Collection of Statistics Act.

The official professional post is Chief Statistician of India (CSI); 'National Statistician' was the role recommended in the report, not the current designation. The Collection of Statistics Act, 2008 replaced the 1953 Act and was amended in 2017. The permanent NSC was created by resolution dated 1 June 2005 and formally constituted in July 2006, but it was not established by an Act of Parliament. The 2019 NSC mandate includes statistical audit; the sources checked do not establish whether a regular audit cycle operated, so do not state that audits were never instituted.

The first National Statistical Commission, constituted in 2006, was chaired by Suresh Tendulkar — the same economist who chaired the 2009 poverty committee. Candidates who learn the two names separately miss that they are one person, and a matching question will exploit it.

C. Rangarajan chaired both the 2000–01 Commission on the statistical system and the 2012–14 expert group on poverty estimation. A question naming 'the Rangarajan Committee' without context is usually about poverty; one naming 'the Rangarajan Commission' is usually about the statistical system. Read the subject, not the name.

flow.caption: Seventy years of reviews, and what each produced

scenes.title: The poverty line committees, in order
scenes.objective: Carry the five poverty committees with their years, chairs and the one thing each changed.

blocks.body: V. M. Dandekar and N. Rath anchored the poverty line to a calorie norm — 2,250 calories a day — and asked what expenditure buys that, separately for rural and urban areas, using NSS consumption data. The calorie anchor begins here.
The Planning Commission task force under Y. K. Alagh fixed rural and urban poverty lines from nutritional requirements and the consumption expenditure that met them, updated for inflation.

D. T. Lakdawala's expert group kept the calorie-based basket but introduced state-specific poverty lines, updated using CPI for Industrial Workers and CPI for Agricultural Labourers, and dropped the practice of scaling NSS consumption to National Accounts aggregates. Its approach was adopted by the government in 1997.

Suresh Tendulkar's expert group moved away from the calorie anchor altogether, used a single poverty line basket common to rural and urban areas, included private spending on health and education, changed the price adjustment, and used a mixed reference period for consumption.

C. Rangarajan's expert group, appointed after the controversy over the Tendulkar line, proposed its own methodology, examined the gap between NSS consumption and the National Accounts, and raised the estimate: poverty in 2011-12 at 29.5% against Tendulkar's lower figure.

blocks.h: The order, and the two that are easy to swap
blocks.body: Dandekar–Rath 1971, Alagh 1979, Lakdawala 1993, Tendulkar 2009, Rangarajan 2014. Lakdawala and Tendulkar are the pair most often reversed; the way to hold them is that Lakdawala kept calories and Tendulkar abandoned them, and abandonment came later.

nodes.label: Tendulkar 2009: drops calories, adds health and education

scenario.teaser: A committee changed a definition and tens of millions of people crossed a line without moving.
scenario.title: What a poverty line actually decides
body: When an expert group changes the basket, the calorie anchor or the price index used to update a poverty line, the measured headcount moves. Nobody's consumption has changed. What has changed is the instrument.

This is not a technicality, because the number is used. Poverty estimates have informed the allocation of central funds to states, the targeting of subsidised food, and the political argument about whether a decade of growth reached the poor. A line drawn one way and another way produces two different countries on paper.

The Tendulkar line drew intense criticism for being too low, which is why the Rangarajan group was appointed and why its higher estimate for the same year, 29.5% for 2011-12, mattered so much. Two committees, one dataset, two answers — both defensible, because the disagreement is about definition rather than arithmetic.

For the paper, carry the sequence and what each changed. For understanding, carry this: when a statistic has consequences, the committee that defines it is doing something closer to policy than to measurement, which is exactly why the independence of statistical bodies keeps coming back as a question.
scenario.close: A poverty line is a decision wearing the clothes of a measurement.

scenes.title: The law behind the numbers
scenes.objective: State what the Collection of Statistics Act does and what the 2017 amendment changed.

blocks.body: The statute that gives legal backing to the collection of statistics in India. It replaced the Collection of Statistics Act of 1953, and its enactment was one of the Rangarajan Commission's recommendations that the government did act on. It empowers the appropriate government to collect statistics on economic, demographic, social, scientific and environmental matters, and it protects the confidentiality of the information given.

blocks.h: The Collection of Statistics (Amendment) Act, 2017 — three changes
blocks.body: First, jurisdiction: the Act now extends to the whole of India, with a proviso applying it to Jammu and Kashmir only for matters in the Union and Concurrent Lists. Second, nodal officers: a new section 3A requires the Central Government, each State Government and each Union territory administration to designate an officer to coordinate and supervise statistical activities in that government. Third, use of information: section 9(1) was amended so that information furnished may be used for statistical purposes in the prescribed manner.

blocks.h: What the amendment did not do
blocks.body: It did not create a statutory National Statistical Commission, and it did not change the penalty structure of the 2008 Act. A question that attributes either to the 2017 amendment is wrong, and both are tempting.

The Collection of Statistics Act is a statute passed by Parliament. The National Statistical Commission is a resolution of the executive. Both concern official statistics; only one is law. Keeping these apart answers a surprising share of this module.

scenes.title: The 2024 Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys
scenes.objective: Describe the 2024 NSS Steering Committee, its remit and the limits of what is known about its post-June 2026 status.

blocks.body: The Ministry's reply states that no Standing Committee on Economic Statistics (SCES) existed as of that date and confirms an order dated 14 June 2024 constituting a 17-member Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys.

The Steering Committee was chaired by the Chairperson of the National Statistical Commission, had 17 members and a non-member secretary, and was given an original two-year tenure. Its terms of reference covered NSS surveys, including survey design, questionnaires, sampling, methods, concepts, definitions and tabulation plans.

The originally notified two-year tenure reached its end in June 2026. No official extension or reconstitution order was located in the primary sources checked by 14 November 2026. Do not describe the committee as currently active without a later order.

blocks.h: Do not infer a direct successor
blocks.body: The official reply confirms the NSS-specific Steering Committee and says no SCES existed as of July 2024. It does not by itself establish that the committee inherited every function of the SCoS or confirm a formal SCoS dissolution date. Do not assert a full SCES-to-SCoS-to-dissolution sequence without the relevant orders.

Distinguish a permanent advisory commission created by resolution from a time-limited survey-specific committee. A two-year tenure notified in June 2024 cannot automatically be treated as current in November 2026.

scenario.teaser: A Ministry reply in July 2024 confirms a 17-member committee for National Sample Surveys with a two-year tenure.
scenario.title: The 2024 Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys
body: In its Lok Sabha reply dated 24 July 2024, MoSPI confirmed that an order dated 14 June 2024 had constituted a Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys. The reply also stated that no SCES existed as of 24 July 2024.

The Steering Committee was chaired by the Chairperson of the National Statistical Commission, comprised 17 members, had a non-member secretary and an original two-year tenure. Its remit covered the methodology and implementation of NSS surveys.

The original two-year tenure reached its end in June 2026. No official extension or reconstitution order was located in the primary sources checked by 14 November 2026. Its status after that date therefore remains unverified.

The official reply does not establish that this committee was a direct successor to every function of the SCoS, nor does it prove the date or terms of a formal SCoS dissolution. Avoid presenting the media-reported chronology as an official legal sequence.
scenario.close: For current-affairs questions, use the date and terms of the actual MoSPI order, and verify any extension before calling a time-limited committee current.

scenes.title: Attribute each change to the right body
scenes.objective: Apply the two sequences rather than recite them.
scenes.problem: Name the committee or commission responsible for each: (a) introducing state-specific poverty lines updated by CPI-IW and CPI-AL; (b) recommending a statutory apex statistical body accountable to Parliament; (c) building India's first official national accounts; (d) dropping the calorie anchor and adding private health and education spending to the poverty basket; (e) recommending a single agency for the population and economic censuses, with provincial statisticians.
hints: Sort them first into two families: the poverty line, and the design of the statistical system itself.
Three of the five are poverty committees; one is a system review from the 2000s; one is from the colonial period.
For (a) and (d), the question is which came first — the one that kept calories or the one that dropped them.

solution.say: (a) The Lakdawala expert group of 1993, whose approach the government adopted in 1997.
solution.math: State-specific lines, CPI-IW and CPI-AL → Lakdawala 1993

solution.say: (b) The Rangarajan Commission of 2000–01, which reported in August 2001.
solution.math: Statutory apex body → Rangarajan Commission 2001 (not implemented)

solution.say: (c) The National Income Committee of 1949, chaired by Mahalanobis with Gadgil and Rao.

solution.math: No calorie anchor, health and education included → Tendulkar 2009

scenes.answer: Lakdawala 1993; Rangarajan Commission 2001; National Income Committee 1949; Tendulkar 2009; Bowley–Robertson 1930s.
scenes.check: If you attributed (b) to the National Statistical Commission itself, you have confused the body that recommended with the body that resulted — and the resulting body is precisely the one that did not get the statutory status.

scenes.title: Six statements — verdict on each before you look
scenes.objective: Meet the wordings that turn a true fact false.
scenes.intro: Each is the standard fact or a single-word corruption of it.

items.claim: The Rangarajan Commission of 2001 recommended a statutory apex statistical body, and the government implemented that recommendation in full.
items.why: It recommended a statutory body accountable to Parliament. What was created, by resolution in 2005, was a non-statutory National Statistical Commission. The statutory form was never enacted.

items.claim: The National Income Committee of 1949 was chaired by P. C. Mahalanobis.
items.why: With D. R. Gadgil and V. K. R. V. Rao as members. Its first report came in April 1951 and its final report in 1954.

items.claim: The Tendulkar committee of 2009 retained the calorie norm as the basis of the poverty line.
items.why: Tendulkar moved away from the calorie anchor, used a common poverty line basket and included private spending on health and education. It was Lakdawala, in 1993, who kept the calorie-based basket.

items.claim: Suresh Tendulkar chaired both the first National Statistical Commission and a poverty estimation committee.
items.why: He chaired the first NSC constituted in 2006 and the poverty expert group that reported in 2009. One person, two well-known bodies.

items.claim: The Standing Committee on Statistics was renamed the Standing Committee on Economic Statistics in 2023.
items.why: Do not infer a formal renaming or dissolution sequence from secondary reporting. The primary MoSPI reply of 24 July 2024 states that no SCES existed as of that date and confirms the 14 June 2024 order for a separate NSS Steering Committee.

items.claim: The Collection of Statistics (Amendment) Act, 2017 requires central, state and union territory governments to designate nodal officers for statistical activities.
items.why: That is the new section 3A inserted by the amendment, alongside the change to the Act's jurisdiction.

scenes.title: Transfer — a case the lesson has not shown you
scenes.objective: Reason from the pattern to a situation the lesson did not cover.
scenes.problem: Suppose the government today appointed a new expert committee to revise the poverty line using the HCES 2022-23 data. Predict three things: what the committee would have to decide, whether its conclusions would bind anyone, and what would determine whether its line is accepted.
hints: Look back at what each previous committee actually had to settle. The list is short and it repeats.
Ask what kind of body it would be, and recall what every such body in this topic can and cannot do.
The last part is not statistical. Think about what happened to the Tendulkar line.

solution.say: What it must decide: whether to anchor on calories or on a broader basket; whether rural and urban lines come from one basket or two; which price index updates the line over time; whether private health and education spending are counted; and which reference period for consumption to use.
solution.math: Basket · anchor · price index · inclusions · reference period

solution.say: Whether it binds: no. It would be an expert group or committee, advising. The line becomes official only if the government accepts it, exactly as Lakdawala's approach was adopted in 1997 and Rangarajan's 2014 recommendations were not acted on in the same way.
solution.math: Committee → recommends; government → adopts or shelves

solution.say: What determines acceptance: partly technical scrutiny, and partly the consequences of the number. A line that raises the headcount sharply has fiscal and political costs; one that lowers it invites the charge of defining poverty away. The Tendulkar episode is the precedent.

scenes.answer: It would settle basket, anchor, price index, inclusions and reference period; it would only recommend; and acceptance would turn on technical scrutiny together with what the resulting number costs politically.
scenes.check: If your second answer was that the committee's line automatically becomes the official poverty line, re-read what happened to the Rangarajan 2014 report.

scenes.title: What you should now be able to do unaided
scenes.objective: Compress both sequences to what survives to the exam hall.
body: The system reviews: Bowley and Robertson in the 1930s (one agency, provincial statisticians); the National Income Committee of 1949 under Mahalanobis with Gadgil and Rao (national accounts, first report 1951, final 1954); the Rangarajan Commission constituted in 2000 and reporting in August 2001.

What Rangarajan asked for and what arrived: a statutory body accountable to Parliament, a National Statistician, regular audits, a reformed Act. Delivered: the National Statistician, and the Collection of Statistics Act 2008. Not delivered: the statutory commission — the NSC exists by resolution of 2005, effective 2006 — and the audits.
The first NSC, 2006, was chaired by Suresh Tendulkar, who also chaired the 2009 poverty expert group.

The poverty line: Dandekar–Rath 1971 (2,250 calories), Alagh 1979 (nutrition-based lines), Lakdawala 1993 (state-specific lines, CPI-IW and CPI-AL, adopted 1997), Tendulkar 2009 (no calorie anchor, health and education in, mixed reference period), Rangarajan 2014 (new method, 29.5% for 2011-12).
The law: Collection of Statistics Act 2008, replacing the 1953 Act; the 2017 amendment extends jurisdiction, inserts section 3A on nodal officers, and amends section 9(1) on the use of information.

The recent machinery: MoSPI's 24 July 2024 Lok Sabha reply states that no SCES existed as of that date and confirms a separate 17-member Steering Committee for National Sample Surveys, constituted by order dated 14 June 2024. Its original tenure was two years. Do not claim that it inherited every SCoS function or that a formal SCoS dissolution date is established by this reply.
